mainTopic: Whether a poured stream (נצוק) connects for melted foods, and the size of a 'full ladle of רקב'
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה, where בית שמאי add thick bean stews to the list of liquids whose poured stream counts as connected. רמי בר חמא asks whether melted foods also get this stream connection. The answer depends on whether the משנה's reason is that those liquids pull back or simply that they are thick. רבא tries to prove it from melted fat of a dead body, but רבי זירא explains that case as fat that hardened into one piece. רבינא tries a proof from בית שמאי's wording, and רב אשי answers that honey and stew connect for different reasons. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's 'full ladle of רקב'. חזקיה says it is a full palm and רבי יוחנן says it is a full handful. The גמרא matches רבי יוחנן to the חכמים and חזקיה to רבי מאיר. רב שימי בר אדא's question about which direction רבי מאיר meant ends in תיקו.

steps.title: בית שמאי add bean stews to the list
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say a poured stream of thick bean stew also counts as connected, because it pulls back when the pouring stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: Even a stream of stew made from crushed beans or whole beans connects, because it pulls back toward where it came from.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה. בית שמאי add bean stews to the list of thick liquids whose poured stream counts as one connected unit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a poured stream does not connect the pure upper vessel to the impure lower vessel. Thick liquids are different, because when you stop pouring, part of the stream pulls back up. That pull-back shows the stream acts like one piece, and בית שמאי say bean stew behaves this way too.

keyTerms.meaning: It pulls back, returning toward its source

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַמִּקְפָּה שֶׁל גְּרִיסִין וְשֶׁל פּוֹל,
phrases.english: Even a stew of crushed beans or of whole beans [connects],
phrases.notes: The word 'connects' carries over from earlier in the משנה, which lists thick liquids whose stream counts as joined.

phrases.english: because it pulls back toward its source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of liquids whose stream connects
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית שמאי, the poured stream of a thick bean stew counts as connected, because it pulls back.

steps.title: Does the stream rule apply to foods?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether melted foods also get the 'stream connection.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: Is there a stream connection for foods, or is there no stream connection for foods?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a question. רמי בר חמא asks whether the rule of a connected stream also applies to melted foods, such as melted fat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only discussed certain thick liquids. The question is whether solid foods that were melted and poured out are treated the same way. The next step explains why this is a real doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked, raising a real question
A poured stream that joins the upper and lower vessels

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
Is there a stream connection for foods,
or is there no stream connection for foods?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the משנה's stream rule and asks whether it reaches melted foods
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether melted foods poured from vessel to vessel count as connected the way thick liquids do

steps.title: The two sides of the question
steps.stepSummary: Is the משנה's reason that those liquids flow back, which foods don't do? Or is it that they are thick, which melted foods also are?
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say [those liquids connect] because they have a flow that pulls back, and these foods have no such flow? Or perhaps it is because they are thick, and here these foods are also thick?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רמי בר חמא is unsure. It lays out two possible reasons for the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is the pull-back flow, melted foods do not connect, since they don't flow back. If the reason is thickness, melted foods do connect, since they are thick too. The answer depends on which reason is the real one.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say? This opens the first side of a doubt
A flowing, stringy stream that pulls back
Or perhaps? This opens the second side

phrases.english: Do we say
[those liquids connect] because they have a flow that pulls back,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the honey and batter listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: and these [foods] don't have such a flow?
Or perhaps it is because they are thick,
and here these are thick too?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית בְּהוּ רִירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two reasons behind רמי בר חמא's question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason for the משנה's rule the pull-back flow, or the thickness?
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole question rests on finding the true reason for the משנה. The two possible reasons lead to opposite results for melted foods.

steps.title: רבא's proof from melted fat of a dead body
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: whole fat of a dead body that was melted stays impure. He argues this shows there is a stream connection for foods.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear: Fat of a dead body that was whole, and one melted it, is impure. If it was in separate pieces and one melted it, it is pure. And if you think there is no stream connection for foods, then whole fat that was melted should also be pure!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא tries to answer רמי בר חמא from a ברייתא about melting fat from a dead body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fat that was one whole piece, the size of a כזית, stays impure even after it is melted. Melted fat spreads out and flows, so if foods had no stream connection, the parts would count as separate pieces, each too small to make it impure. Since it stays impure, רבא concludes that melted foods do count as connected.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters your mind, meaning 'if you thought'

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:
Fat of a dead body that is whole
phrases.notes: 'Whole' means one piece the size of a כזית, the amount needed to make things impure.

phrases.english: and one melted it — it is impure.
If it was in separate pieces and one melted it — it is pure.
And if you were to think
there is no stream connection for foods,
then whole fat that was melted should also be pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle רמי בר חמא's question
steps.raayaObject: That there is a stream connection for foods
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: whole fat of a dead body that was melted stays impure

steps.title: רבי זירא: the fat stuck together at the rim
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא explains that the ברייתא is a case where the melted fat rose up and hardened together, so it was never a flowing stream at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: I and מר son of רבינא explained it: What case are we dealing with here? Where, while he was heating it, the flame rose up to the mouth of the pot and the fat hardened there, so it is all together.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא rejects רבא's proof. He says the ברייתא is about a special case that has nothing to do with a stream.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא's case, the heat pushed the fat up to the rim of the pot, where it hardened into one solid mass. Since it stayed one piece, there was never a stream to discuss, and it is impure for that reason. So the ברייתא proves nothing about whether foods have a stream connection, and רמי בר חמא's question is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: With what case are we dealing here? This limits a source to a special case
A column of fire, the flame rising up

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said:
I and Mar son of Ravina explained it:
What case are we dealing with here?
Where, while he was heating it,
the column of fire rose to the mouth of the pot
and [the fat] hardened,
so that it is all together.
phrases.notes: It stayed one solid mass and never flowed, so there was no stream to talk about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: אֲנָא וּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבִינָא תַּרְגֵּימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes away רבא's proof by limiting the ברייתא to a special case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof; the question itself stays open
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is about fat that hardened into one piece at the rim, not fat that flowed, so it says nothing about a stream
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof from melted fat fails, because the ברייתא can be read as fat that stayed one solid piece. The question of whether melted foods have a stream connection is still unanswered.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying the fat is pure. It is still impure, but only because it stayed one piece, not because of any stream connection.

steps.title: רבינא tries a proof from בית שמאי's bean stew
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings בית שמאי's reason for the bean stew, 'because they pull back,' as a proof for רמי בר חמא's question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear. בית שמאי say: even thick stew of crushed beans or of whole beans counts as connected, because they pull back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא tries to answer רמי בר חמא's question from the wording of the משנה itself. בית שמאי's reason for the stew is that it pulls back when you pour it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא reasons that the whole מחלוקת is about whether something 'pulls back.' So the reason the משנה's thick liquids count as connected is that they pull back, not just that they are thick. Melted foods, which do not pull back, would then not get the stream connection.

keyTerms.meaning: They pull back: the poured stream draws back up when the pouring stops

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear:
Beit Shammai say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף הַמִּקְפָּה שֶׁל גְּרִיסִין וְשֶׁל פּוֹל —
phrases.english: Even a stew of crushed beans or of whole beans,
phrases.notes: He is quoting the same line of the משנה we saw in Step 1.

phrases.english: because they pull back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא's proof was pushed off in Step 5, a new proof is offered for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That the reason for the stream connection is 'pulling back,' which bears on melted foods
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording of בית שמאי: מפני שהן סולדין לאחוריהן

steps.title: Honey's reason is different from בית שמאי's reason for stew
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rejects the proof: honey counts because it is thick, while בית שמאי's stew counts because it pulls back.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these the same? There (honey and the like), it is because they are thick. Here (the stew), it is because of the flowing that pulls back.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes away רבינא's proof. He says the two cases are not the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honey may count as connected simply because it is thick. בית שמאי's stew needs a different reason, the pulling back. So the stew's reason tells us nothing about the reason for honey, and the question about melted foods stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? A way of saying the two cases are different
Strings of flowing liquid that pull back

phrases.english: Are these comparable?
There, it is because they are thick.
phrases.notes: 'There' means honey and the other liquids the משנה lists.

phrases.english: Here, it is because of the flowing strands.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. The question about melted foods is left open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Honey and stew connect for different reasons, so the reason given for the stew cannot tell us the reason for honey.
steps.whatToRemember: No proof was found either way, so we still do not know whether melted foods get the stream connection.

steps.title: How big is a full ladle of decayed dust?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's 'full ladle of רקב' and asks how big that measure is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and for a full ladle of רקב.' How big is this measure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about a נזיר becoming impure from a ladle-full of decayed dust of a dead body. It asks how much that is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This opens a completely new topic. The question is simply a measurement question: what amount counts as a 'ladle-full.'

keyTerms.meaning: Decayed dust of a dead body

phrases.english: "And for a full ladle of decayed dust."
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה: a נזיר must shave for becoming impure from this amount.

phrases.english: And how much is its measure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stream topic and begins a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of the 'full ladle of רקב.'

steps.title: חזקיה says a palm, רבי יוחנן says a handful
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the amount is a full palm. רבי יוחנן says it is a full handful.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: as much as fills the palm of the hand. רבי יוחנן said: a full handful.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the question with two different sizes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה measures by what sits on the flat palm. רבי יוחנן measures by what the whole hand, fingers included, can hold, which is a bigger amount.

keyTerms.meaning: His handful, held with the whole hand

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said: a full palm of the hand.
Rabbi Yochanan said: a full handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8 with two opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיה: a full palm. רבי יוחנן: a full handful.

steps.title: A teaching where רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a teaching: רבי מאיר says the ladle is measured from the base of the fingers and up, and the חכמים say it is a handful.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: the full ladle of רקב that they spoke of is measured from the base of the fingers and up. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: a full handful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an older source on the same measure. It is setting up the next move, checking which side each אמורא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים's opinion matches רבי יוחנן word for word. רבי מאיר's opinion sounds like it measures only the fingers, which seems to match neither אמורא.

keyTerms.meaning: The base of the fingers, where they meet the palm

phrases.english: We learned: the full ladle of decayed dust that they spoke of
is from the base of the fingers and upward.
These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: a full handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an earlier source to test the two opinions of Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: Which earlier opinion each אמורא follows
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching recording the מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and the חכמים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: the 'full ladle of רקב' is measured from the base of the fingers and up. The חכמים: a full handful.

steps.title: Whose opinion does חזקיה follow?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן follows the חכמים, but חזקיה seems to follow neither רבי מאיר nor the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי יוחנן said his view like the חכמים. But חזקיה, whom does he follow? Not רבי מאיר and not the חכמים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חזקיה, because his palm measure does not seem to match either opinion in the teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say a handful, like רבי יוחנן. רבי מאיר seems to mean the fingers only. חזקיה's palm is neither, so it looks like he has no earlier source behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense: one side is fine, the problem is with the other
Like whom? Whose opinion does he follow?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: It makes sense that Rabbi Yochanan spoke like the Rabbis.
But Chizkiyah, like whom?
Not like Rabbi Meir and not like the Rabbis!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבָּנַן. אֶלָּא חִזְקִיָּה כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the teaching of Step 10 to challenge חזקיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's measure of a full palm
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His measure does not match either opinion in the earlier teaching, so it seems to have no source.

steps.title: A full palm equals רבי מאיר's measure
steps.stepSummary: The answer: a full palm and 'from the finger joints and up' are the same measure, so חזקיה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: a full palm and a full measure from the finger joints and up are one and the same measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that חזקיה really does agree with רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we see that the palm and רבי מאיר's measure are the same amount, חזקיה is no longer alone. He follows רבי מאיר, just as רבי יוחנן follows the חכמים.

phrases.english: They say: a full palm of the hand
and a full measure from his finger joints upward
are one measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: מְלֹא פִּיסַּת הַיָּד וּמְלֹא קִשְׁרֵי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו לְמַעְלָה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that two measures that sound different are really the same
steps.terutzHavaAmina: חזקיה's palm is a different measure from רבי מאיר's finger measure.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are the same measure, so חזקיה follows רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Which direction is 'upward'?
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר אדא asks how we know רבי מאיר's 'from the joints and up' means toward the fingertips. Maybe it means the other way, toward the palm.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר אדא said to רב פפא: How do we know that 'from his finger joints and up' means toward the tips? Maybe it means below that, which would be a full palm?
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר אדא questions the starting point of the challenge against חזקיה. He asks which direction רבי מאיר meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 11 assumed רבי מאיר meant the fingers, toward the tips. If 'up' instead means the other direction, toward the arm, then רבי מאיר is simply describing the palm. In that case חזקיה matches him directly, with no need for the answer in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: Toward the top, meaning the fingertips

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אַדָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Adda said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי מִקִּשְׁרֵי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו וּלְמַעְלָה לְרֹאשׁ?
phrases.english: From where do we know that this 'from his finger joints and up' means toward the tips?
Perhaps it means below it,
phrases.notes: 'Below' means from the joints back toward the arm, the palm area.

phrases.english: so that it would be a full palm of the hand?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי מִקִּשְׁרֵי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו וּלְמַעְלָה לְרֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reading of רבי מאיר's words that the challenge in Step 11 relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'upward' in רבי מאיר's words points toward the fingertips or toward the palm.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Up' here is not about height. The question is which direction along the hand רבי מאיר meant: toward the fingertips, or back toward the palm.

steps.title: The question stays unanswered
steps.stepSummary: No answer is found, and the question is left standing: תיקו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion without answering רב שימי בר אדא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not know which direction רבי מאיר meant. So the question about the exact meaning of his measure is left open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: חזקיה says a palm and רבי יוחנן says a handful. רבי יוחנן follows the חכמים. חזקיה is matched to רבי מאיר, but exactly what רבי מאיר's words mean stays unresolved (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes Step 13's question without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether רבי מאיר's 'from the finger joints and up' means the fingers or the palm remains unresolved.
